terms.grammar: verb, first conjugation, transitive; with accusative and infinitive
terms.comment: The everyday “forbid”: vetō tē abīre. Vetitum is “forbidden”.

terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation; with dative of the person, ablative of the thing, or nē
evidence: Caes. B.G. 5.22: interdīcit atque imperat Cassivellaunō nē (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: An official prohibition: a magistrate’s or a parent’s order.
The noun “a ban”; in law, a praetor’s interdict.

phrases.latin: num litterās quoque … ab senātū adfers quae mē rem gerere vetant?
phrases.english: are you bringing a letter from the senate too, forbidding me to act?

phrases.latin: et ācta agimus, quod vetāmur vetere prōverbiō
phrases.english: and we are doing what is done already, which an old proverb forbids

sources: Lewis & Short: veto · Lewis & Short: interdico · Lewis & Short: interdictum
